pages.text: Put a $(item)Local Weather Station$() up high in the open. Right click it for the wind and gusts, temperature, humidity, pressure and the rain in the last hour (it only catches rain with open sky above it).$(br2)It has no radio of its own: anything that wants weather takes the nearest one within $(thing)64 blocks$(), as many devices at once as you like.

pages.title: What reads it
pages.text: An $(l:radiocraft:digital/aprs)H19$() or $(l:radiocraft:digital/headless_tnc)Headless APRS TNC$() sends its weather in its beacons (the WX symbol). A $(l:radiocraft:sky/weather_observer)Weather Observer$() sends it through any radio. A $(l:radiocraft:sky/weather_display)Local Weather Station Display$() shows it on a red LCD, and an FM broadcast transmitter on its data wire reads it out.

pages.title: Real weather
pages.text: With plain Minecraft weather there is no wind. With $(thing)Another Weather Mod$() installed the weather is local: moving storms, wind, hail and hurricanes, and the charts and reports describe them.$(br2)Strong winds (over 33 m/s) can blow antenna parts and wire holders down. Rain halves a solar panel's output where it falls, and severe weather halves it again.
